To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the IFPs expressed in the peripheral nervous system are not only important for the maintenance of axonal caliber and axonal transport, as previously thought, but they are also involved in the development and regeneration of peripheral nerves, in the formation and maintenance of synapses and in the response to injuries.
the expression of IFPs is not restricted to the central and peripheral neurons, but is also found in the glial cells and muscles.
the expression of IFPs in the peripheral nervous system is highly dynamic and that the expression of different IFPs in the same tissue is highly plastic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression, function and regulation of IFPs in the peripheral nervous system and in other related tissues.
the role of IFPs in peripheral neurons, and with how they are modified during neuronal development and in response to injury.
the expression and function of IFPs in normal and pathological states of the peripheral nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IFPs are expressed in a highly specific manner in the peripheral nervous system and in its associated structures, and that they are involved in the pathogenesis of several diseases.
IFPs are expressed in the peripheral nervous system in a complex manner, and their expression can be modified in response to injury.
the IFPs are not simply structural elements of cells, but are also involved in the regulation of cell functions, and that their expression is highly regulated in normal and pathological situations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the peripheral nervous system: (i) the IFPs expressed in neurons and glia during development, and in adult tissues after an injury response are different; (ii) the distribution and the relative amounts of the different IFPs are not uniform, and (iii) their expression is not static but dynamic.

, in the peripheral nervous system: (1) IFPs are expressed during development, in cell differentiation and during injury responses; (2) their expression is regulated in a cell-specific manner; (3) they are involved in cell-cell interactions; and (4) their expression is altered in several diseases, such as motor neuron disease and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, in which IFP dysfunction is likely to play a role in disease progression.
IFPs are expressed in a tissue-specific manner, and that their expression can be modulated during the development and in response to injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IFPs are not static structures in cells, but are dynamic, and their expression and organization change in a cell-specific manner, and are modulated by a number of factors, including injury.
IFPs are expressed by different cells during development and in adult tissues.
the study of the IFP network is essential for the comprehension and diagnosis of many diseases, including peripheral neuropathies.
